findings.desc: [codex-host-2, verified] Pass-bucket mutations can no-op and still 'conform'. For acceptanceBucket/acknowledgedLimitations classes (expected status:pass), tamper.mjs asserts verifyStatus==pass + fingerprintMatch against the frozen pass fingerprint, but does NOT assert the mutation actually CHANGED the corpus. If a malicious mutation silently no-ops (e.g. gold-weaken-expectedids finds no query with expectedIds.length>1), verify passes on the CLEAN corpus and the clean fingerprint equals the acknowledged-limitation pass fingerprint -> the harness emits conforming H2 blind-spot evidence for a tamper that was never applied. Fix: re-derive the byte-diff signal (records/gold/manifest changed vs clean) per class and assert the mutation genuinely applied (non-dropped classes MUST change the corpus), failing loudly on a no-op.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in 4fadf4f40. tamper.mjs now computes a per-class byteDiff vs clean and re-derives the M0 disposition; every non-dropped class must show a real byteDiff (records/gold/manifest changed) or it fails loudly — a silent no-op can no longer masquerade as a conforming blind spot. Verified: no-op mutations=0.

findings.desc: [codex-host-2, verified] dropped entries bypass the dropped-semantics check. For the dropped class (seed-swap[refreshed]) tamper.mjs records fingerprintMatch:null, takes disposition from the frozen bucket, and checks only verifyStatus==pass. If the mutation drifts to a no-op or another pass-producing change (e.g. gold-additive-field), it is silently mis-recorded as a valid dropped case. Fix: for dropped, assert the DEFINING property — records.jsonl AND gold-queries.json byte-identical to clean (only manifest metadata changed) — not merely verifyStatus==pass.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in 4fadf4f40. dropped classes now assert the defining property (records.jsonl AND gold-queries.json byte-identical to clean) instead of only verifyStatus==pass; drift to a pass-producing change fails loudly. Verified: dropped-semantics violations=0 (seed-swap recordsChanged=false goldChanged=false).

findings.desc: CHK-001:adversarial:0 (priority=should) has no bound verificationEvidence — validate reports status:missing for this intentRef. Independently confirmed the underlying claim is TRUE (27 unique iterationIds in tamper-verdicts.jsonl, each matching protocol.iterationIdRule format tamper/<scale>/<class>/<manifestHandling>; all 27 frozen tamperMatrix classes appear exactly once, 0 missing/0 extra/0 duplicates), but no verificationEvidence entry was ever recorded against CHK-001:adversarial:0 to bind that proof into the audit trail. Advisory (should-priority, not a must-gap): add a verificationEvidence entry for CHK-001:adversarial:0 citing this check so validate stops reporting it missing.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed. CHK-001:adversarial:0 now has bound verification evidence: 27 lines / 27 unique iterationIds (tamper/small/<class>/<handling>), every frozen-matrix class exactly once, 0 dup/missing/extra.

findings.desc: conformance-logic-gap: tamper.mjs:277-332 compareFingerprint() only special-cases frozen metric predicate op=="<" (threshold form); build-protocol.mjs:136-150 metricPredicate() can also emit op:">" (false-surface-rate gold=0 cases) and an op:"!=" fallback form, but compareFingerprint has no branch for ">" or "!=" and silently falls through to raw epsilon equality against the frozen VALUE for those forms (no threshold-direction check at all). Verified against the committed protocol.json: only "==" and "<" ops actually occur today (no false-surface metric ever went above 0 in this matrix), so this does not currently cause a false PASS or false FAIL. But the code comment at tamper.mjs:17-21 and 262-271 claims the comparison "honor[s] the frozen predicate form" for numeric metrics generally, which is not implemented for ">"/"!=". If protocol.json is ever regenerated against different fixtures and a false-surface metric produces an observed value >0 (a genuinely malicious tamper this instrument is meant to catch), compareFingerprint would not enforce the ">" threshold direction — only numeric closeness to the frozen value — a latent correctness gap in the exact logic (predicate-form fidelity) this M1 harness exists to police.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in 4fadf4f40. compareFingerprint now handles ==, <, >, != with epsilon+threshold guards and THROWS on any unrecognized op (no more silent epsilon-equality for >/!=). Only ==/< occur in today's frozen protocol so current behavior is unchanged; the latent gap is closed and the overclaiming comments corrected.

findings.desc: quality: experiments/pos-instrument-replay/tamper.mjs:370-405 -- compareFingerprint's new numeric predicate branches for op '>' and op 'not-equal' (plus the default:throw-on-unknown-op branch) are never exercised by any test. The frozen protocol.json's 27 tamperMatrix entries only ever produce failureSignals with op 'equals' (4 entries) or op 'less-than' (12 entries) -- zero entries use the 'greater-than' or 'not-equal' ops (confirmed by iterating protocol.json's tamperMatrix programmatically). selfcheck-m1.mjs's negative test (lines 180-256) only flips a boolean flag, not a numeric metric predicate op, so it does not exercise these branches either. F-004's claim that compareFingerprint covers all four predicate ops and throws on an unknown op is true of the written code but 3 of its 4 op branches (greater-than, not-equal, and the throw-on-unknown-op default) are untested -- a latent bug there would not be caught by the current test suite.
